agent_notes: 'At that time' (21:22) is ambiguous: Rashbam says at Isaac's birth, Radak at the birth or the weaning. Revised after review: I first anchored it on the rescue's end with a 1-year margin, which excluded the birth reading. Now it is anchored on the birth with offset 1 year and margin 18 months, so the span covers both the birth (Rashbam) and the weaning (Radak). The text order would put it after the rescue, but 'at that time' is not a sequence marker, so the timeline may show it before the weaning feast. The place of the talks is not stated; Abraham is at Beer-sheba by 21:31–32 (Beer-sheba to Philistia, about 54 km straight line; the return of Abimelech and Phicol is not given its own event).

agent_notes: 'Many days' (21:34) is a MACRO_ERA span. Rashi counts 26 years in Philistia (after 25 years at Hebron, ending 12 years before the binding), which I take as the duration with a margin of 10 years. I anchor it on the start of the move to Gerar (Gen 20:1, c. 2067 BCE) and let it run 26 years. Radak reads the many days as the rest of Abraham's residence in the Negev. The sojourn overlaps the earlier events of the chapter by design.

agent_notes: Weaning age is not stated. Offset 2 years with margin 1 year: a nursing span of about two years is the usual ancient reading (cf. 1 Sam 1:22–24, which Rashbam cites on 21:8; 2 Macc 7:27 says three). Alternatives of 3 or 5 years would still fall inside the margin to a degree. Ishmael would then be about 16 (born when Abraham was 86, 16:16), which fits 'mocking' (21:9) but is old for being carried (21:14, 'placing it on her shoulder, and the boy'); this is a known tension, not resolved here.

21:20–21 compresses Ishmael's boyhood and marriage. I give it a 10-year duration from the rescue with a 5-year margin; the text offers no figure, so MACRO_ERA. The marriage itself (21:21) is not a separate event because nothing dates it.
